citations.snippet: If the nearly one-third decline on clearcutting recorded by Deter in 2026 is confirmed by Prodes, Brazil will likely post its lowest official deforestation rate since satellite monitoring began in 1988. “The numbers presented today are historic, the result of serious environmental protection policies, and prove that it is entirely possible to fulfill the commitment made by the country to zero and reverse deforestation by 2030,” says Marcio Astrini, executive secretary of the Brazilian NGO Observatório do Clima. [...] Deter uses satellite imagery produced in near real-time to guide environmental inspections done by Ibama (the Brazilian federal environmental agency), but it is “short-sighted” due to its relatively low resolution. Therefore, it is not used to calculate the total deforested area, a function that belongs to another Inpe system, Prodes, whose estimates are published at the end of every year. However, Deter data in the last few years, due to technological improvements, has allowed officials to anticipate how Prodes will behave.
